Based on the strongest evidence available, I'll finalize the report.

## Conclusion

The evidence supports that ivermectin does **not** reduce mortality in COVID-19 patients. The best available data come from large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials rather than the many small, heterogeneous, and often low-quality studies that initially fueled interest in the drug.

**Key evidence:**

- The **TOGETHER trial** (Brazil, published in *NEJM*, 2022), a large, rigorous RCT, found ivermectin did not reduce the risk of hospitalization or emergency department visits compared to placebo in high-risk outpatients with COVID-19 (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869 — note: this specific trial's full report and related ACTIV-6 work reached similar conclusions).

- **ACTIV-6** (JAMA, 2022/2023), a decentralized U.S. platform RCT testing standard and higher-dose (600 mcg/kg) ivermectin in outpatients, found no improvement in time to recovery and did not support ivermectin's use for mild-to-moderate COVID-19 (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2797483).

- A related large NEJM platform trial testing ivermectin alongside metformin and fluvoxamine similarly found no significant benefit on clinical outcomes (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2201662).

- Major health authorities, including the WHO and FDA, do not recommend ivermectin for COVID-19 treatment outside clinical trials, citing insufficient or inconclusive evidence of benefit (https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html).

**Caveats:** Some meta-analyses (e.g., those aggregated on c19early.org) claim positive effects, but these often include lower-quality, non-randomized, or contested studies (including some later retracted or flagged for data integrity issues) and are not considered reliable by mainstream regulatory and scientific bodies. The highest-quality, large-scale RCTs consistently show no mortality benefit, which is the basis for current clinical guidance against using ivermectin for COVID-19.
